claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl bond coat produced from 15–45 μm feedstock has insufficient coating thickness for the thermal-barrier application.
Extending the feedstock particle-size distribution to include particles up to approximately 75 μm will improve effective deposition efficiency.
Including particles up to approximately 75 μm will produce a thicker coating than the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline.
The extended feedstock will preserve coating microstructural integrity relative to the baseline.
The extended feedstock will maintain similarly low as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
Larger feedstock particles have higher thermal inertia than smaller particles.
Larger feedstock particles have greater impact momentum under the proposed spray conditions.
The greater impact momentum of larger particles improves splat formation.
The greater impact momentum of larger particles increases deposition yield.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy and momentum increase coating buildup per spray pass.
Increased particle momentum overcomes inefficient layering while retaining a robust coating microstructure.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger particles limits as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective within the standard processing limits of the existing thermal-spray equipment.
The resulting bond coat will remain suitable under typical high-temperature, oxidizing thermal-barrier-system service conditions.
